title: The Yakut ancestors north along the Lena, c. AD 1000–1500
summary: The Yakut (Sakha) speak a Turkic language and herd horses and cattle in the coldest inhabited basin on earth, around the Lena. Their ancestors came there from the Baikal country in the early second millennium AD, going down the Lena into land held by the Evenki and Yukaghir. The dates and the numbers who moved are argued.

legs.source: Yakuts (Wikipedia): north along the Lena from the Baikal region
legs.doubt: The dates run from the tenth to the fifteenth century in different accounts; the genetic evidence and the Russian records disagree on how large the movement was.

events.label: Lake Baikal country
events.text: The Yakut language's nearest relatives are Turkic languages of southern Siberia, which is why the Baikal and upper Lena are named as where they lived before.

events.label: The Yakutsk basin
events.text: By the time Russians arrived in the 1620s the Yakut were the main people of the middle Lena. Yakutsk was founded there as a fort in 1632.
